title: Keep a mind map for sorting ideas, and publish a diagram that shows how the parts connect.
rule: Use a mind map, a reference form, while a story is being planned: one topic in the middle, its parts on lines around it, and their own parts beyond them. Before it reaches a reader, turn it into the form that shows how the parts relate, a process diagram for steps in order, a hierarchy tree for parts with counts or a table for a list.
use_when: Writers and editors sort the parts of a subject before they know how the parts connect, such as the topics a guide to a city budget might cover.

use_instead.when: The parts follow one another in order
The parts nest inside one another with counts
The parts are a list a reader scans

text: Lines around a center say only that two ideas belong together, not how: one comes before another, sits under it or causes it. A reader needs that relation, which the forms built for it draw.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No kit form: draw a mind map only as a sketch for planning; build process-diagram or hierarchy-tree for a reader.
sketch_alt: A mind map of an illustrative city budget, one topic in the middle with four parts on lines around it and a further idea beside each. The lines say each part belongs to the budget, and nothing about order or size.
